prompt:
Professional fashion photograph, chest-cut demi statue portrait — a sculpted figure ending right at the base of the chest. ONE woman, angled 45 degrees toward the camera, framed so her whole sculpted form is visible from the top of her head down to one single, deliberately carved rounded base right at the base of her chest, well above her waist, her face in natural scale with her body — never an oversized close-up crop of just the face. Where her sculpted form comes to an end there, it is because the sculpture itself ends there, not because a camera frame happens to cut her off.

Subject: A real photograph of a strikingly beautiful adult Italian woman in 1960s Italian film-star makeup — warm olive skin, thick strongly arched dark brows, a long black liner winging up and out at the outer corner of each eye, soft brown eyeshadow, long lashes, large dark eyes with bright real catchlights, a deep red lip with a defined edge, thick glossy dark-brown hair set in a high backcombed style, a smouldering, confident expression. Her whole face, ears and neck are real living flesh with real pores and fine skin grain, real living eyes with bright catchlights and genuine depth, individual hair strands catching the light — a photograph of a real face, not an illustration, not a render, not cel-shaded. On each ear a large real pearl drop with a gold clip.

Piercings: An extreme, overwhelming armour of about one hundred and fifty real metal piercings covering the face and neck: a thick gold septum ring with a smaller ring above it, three gold rings through each nostril and a small stud at the tip of the nose; two straight gold bars across the bridge of the nose between the brows; six thick gold bars stacked through the outer half of each eyebrow; three rows of five small gold studs across the forehead above the brows; six small studs up each temple on the bone, well clear of the eyes; two rows of six small studs along each cheekbone; a gold Medusa stud above the lips with a small stud on each side of it; a big gold hoop, four smaller rings and a snake-bite ring on each side through the lower lip's edge, and six small hoops along the upper lip's edge; a gold labret stud and five rings through the chin; six small studs along each jaw; a column of five small studs down each side of the neck; on each ear a full dense row of twelve big hoops, thick bars, stretched plugs, helix rings and studs from lobe to top; and ten fine gold chains looping from the ear hoops to the nostril rings and the septum ring. The piercings are packed so densely that the rows touch and overlap, leaving only hairline gaps of bare skin between them, until the face reads as a single armour of metal; the eyes and eyelids stay clear. All jewelry is real gold, sitting in real, calm, healthy skin — no redness, no swelling, no irritation — with a small natural warm shadow under each piece. Every piece stays at least a finger's width from the eyeballs, and no chain or bar crosses the eyes.

Piercing depth: every bar and surface bar is embedded in the skin — its middle runs beneath the skin so only its two end studs show on the surface, the skin between them faintly raised over the hidden bar, with a small warm shadow at each end and nothing lying on top of the skin like a sticker. Every ring passes through a small healed opening in the skin, the skin visible through the loop, and every stud sits through the skin with its back hidden. Where a bar, ring or stud goes through the ear, the lip, the nostril or the brow, it passes through the real tissue with the skin wrapping snugly around it.

Physique: A colossal heavy chest wider than her shoulders, broad soft shoulders, thick heavy arms, her upper body filling the frame.

Body: From the collarbones down, her whole body — shoulders, arms, hands, half the chest — is a sculpted vessel of thick, crystal-clear glass in the exact shape of her chest, shoulder and arm, filled completely to the brim so nothing is hollow and there is no air gap. The glass is unmistakably glass: thick, crystal-clear and polished, with bright specular reflections sliding along every curved surface, sharp white highlights and dark refraction edges where the walls are thickest, tiny bubbles trapped in the glass itself. The vessel holds ONE single world, unbroken and continuous through her whole chest: a still snowfall: fine, glowing snowflakes and small warm lights drifting slowly through the clear water. The whole solid form curves inward evenly and seals shut into one single, smooth, rounded base right at the base of her chest — the vessel simply reaching its natural end there, the one rounded base resting flat on the surface beneath her.

Transmission: everything below the collarbones is a transparent material that light passes through, while her real face, ears and neck are opaque living flesh that no light passes through. The background and its light sources are visible straight through her body, bent and tinted by the material, with bright refraction edges and soft coloured shadows. Her face stays completely opaque.

Boundary: a sharp jagged line runs around the base of the neck and across both collarbones — real skin above, material immediately below. There is no line down the centre of her body. At that line, the glass's edge rises in a small raised step above her flesh, casting a crisp shadow — her skin beside it stays smooth and even. The rounded base at her chest is the material's own finish — never the edge of a photograph. Shards interlock along the collarbone line only.

Setting: a huge backdrop behind her washed with two coloured lights from behind — a pale lilac on one side and a soft mint on the other, blending into a smooth gradient in the middle, and a glossy dark floor beneath her.

Pose: her left hand (solid material) resting just below her chest, her right hand (solid material) held at chest height clear of her body, both hands well away from her face, head tilted slightly toward the camera.

Lighting: the glowing backdrop floods her body from behind, so a pale lilac passes through one side and a soft mint passes through the other. A soft frontal light falls on her face and ears only; a thin cool rim light traces her whole figure. shot on a Hasselblad X2D with an 85mm lens, shallow depth of field. 2:3 vertical 8K portrait.
